issue.title: Change in release-asset names breaks automation
issue.body:
Thank you for creating the issue!

- [x] Yes, I'm using a binary release within 2 latest major releases. Only such installations are supported.
- [x] Yes, I've searched similar issues on GitHub and didn't find any.
- [x] Yes, I've included all information below (version, config, etc).


Between 1.26.0 and 1.27.0 the name of the Windows release assets has changed from:
```
golangci-lint-1.26.0-windows-amd64.zip
```
to
```
golangci-lint.exe-1.27.0-windows-amd64.zip
```

This change in format is a pain to manage in automated install scripts as it deviates from what existed before and from the format used for Linux and OSX assets.

It appears that the asset names are generated via `goreleaser` so this might be due to some change in that tool?

It would be very much appreciated if this change was reverted.

body:
I just ran into issues with the docker build, and then learned about `extra_files` (which worked! :tada:).

Do you think it's even necessary to setup a build directory and copy/link files into a temporary directory? I can see advantages for everything, but it seems in order to avoid that the image contains unnecessary/unwanted files, `.dockerignore` is more suitable.

the problem is not dockerignore itself, we do the temp dir thing because, otherwise, the dockerfile would have to `COPY dist/foo_linux_amd64/binary /etc`... and today its just `COPY binary /etc`, which works outside goreleaser as well (`go build . && docker build .`)... 

the linking thing is hacky, ideally we should copy the needed files...

@caarlos0 thanks, I see the reasoning! 👍 

And yeah, maybe a copy is better or less weird on different systems.

Do you have a preference as to what to use:

 - `io.Copy()`,
 - `ioutil.ReadFile()` and `ioutil.WriteFile()`
 - `os.Read()` and `os.Write()`

I am hoping all of them are cross platform? 😂

`io.Copy` copies from a reader to a writer, we still need to create the target file, and there is where the problems happen... 

check https://github.com/golang/go/issues/8868 and specially Rob Pike's comments on https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/go/+/1591
(but IMHO we don't need a perfect 100% correct on all platforms in existence copy file, my plan was to copy the one from that CL 🤣)
Will ignore this for now, as the problem was on github actions and it is working as is for quite some time...
This issue has been automatically locked since there has not been any recent activity after it was closed. Please open a new issue for related bugs.
FWIW: next release will copy the files instead of hard-linking them
